title: Citizen Science Integration Barriers
bottleneck: Millions of volunteers could contribute observations, classification, and distributed computing, but professional science rarely integrates them beyond token projects. Data-quality skepticism, institutional inertia, and lack of funding for coordination infrastructure keep citizen science marginal. Professional researchers often distrust volunteer data, though validation studies frequently show it is reliable.
why_it_blocks: Untapped distributed labor could accelerate data-heavy fields at near-zero marginal cost. Data-hungry fields like ecology and astronomy could scale enormously with volunteer labor. The marginal cost of an additional volunteer observer is near zero.
current_state: Platforms like Zooniverse and iNaturalist prove the model; structural integration into funded research programs is rare. Funding the coordination layer — platforms, training, quality control — would unlock enormous volunteer capacity. The volunteer capacity waiting to be tapped is enormous.
